plans.note: Only the preamble is exposed in the outline; a Kubient-form MSA will almost certainly contain a limitation of liability article (cap plus consequential-damages waiver). Search the full text for 'liability', 'consequential', 'aggregate amount paid' and confirm mutuality of the cap and carve-outs for indemnity, confidentiality, IP infringement and willful misconduct.

Expect an indemnification article in the MSA body. Verify Kubient (as Provider) indemnifies AP for third-party IP infringement, data/privacy breach and its own negligence or willful misconduct, and that any AP-side indemnity is limited to AP-supplied content/materials. Treat as missing only if no indemnity language appears anywhere.

Presence check. Ad-tech MSAs rarely restrict the customer's lines of business, and the visible outline shows no restrictive-covenants section. Scan for 'compete', 'competing business', 'restricted activities'; flag only if a covenant binds AP.

Presence check. Watch for exclusivity smuggled into the services/scope or ad-inventory provisions ('exclusive provider', 'sole source', 'all of Customer's inventory'). Nothing in the visible outline suggests it; confirm AP remains free to use other ad platforms.

Direction check. Look in pricing/fees for 'most favored', 'best rates', 'no less favorable terms'. An MFN running to AP is beneficial and should not be flagged; only an MFN obliging AP to grant Kubient best terms is a deviation.

Frequently sits near confidentiality or general provisions. Check scope (mutual vs. one-way against AP), duration (12 months preferred, 24 fallback), limitation to personnel involved in the engagement, and a general-advertising/unsolicited-response carve-out.

Term and Termination article should be present; 'Initial Term' is already a defined term. Confirm AP may terminate for convenience on reasonable notice (30 days preferred) without penalty or acceleration of unpaid fees, and that Kubient cannot terminate for convenience mid-term.

Tied to the defined 'Initial Term'; look for renewal/extension language in the term provision or an order form/exhibit. Check the non-renewal notice window (30 days preferred, 60 acceptable) and whether renewal pricing is capped; an uncapped uplift is noted, an excessive notice window is the deviation trigger.

Expect a governing law/venue clause in the miscellaneous article; Kubient is New York-based and AP is New York-headquartered, so New York courts are likely and acceptable. Flag only foreign law, mandatory offshore arbitration, or an inconvenient exclusive venue.

Standard miscellaneous provision. Confirm AP may assign to affiliates and to a successor by merger or asset sale without consent, and that Kubient has no termination or consent right triggered by an AP change of control.

Direction check. Critical for AP given its content: verify AP retains ownership of its data, content and any deliverables it pays for, that Kubient's rights are a limited service-delivery licence, and that any aggregated/usage-data or feedback clause does not transfer AP IP or permit identifiable reuse.

Look for the grant of access to the Kubient platform in the services or licence article. Confirm the licence extends to AP affiliates and contractors acting on AP's behalf and is not revocable at Kubient's discretion outside a termination right.

Check fees/compliance provisions for a Kubient right to audit AP usage or records. Test frequency (no more than annually), advance written notice, business-hours/off-site conduct, and Kubient bearing its own cost absent a material underpayment.

Direction check. Service credits or SLA remedies flowing to AP are welcome and should not be flagged. Scan fees/termination language for early-termination fees, shortfall charges or stipulated damages payable by AP.

Look for a representations and warranties article plus any disclaimer. Confirm a professional/workmanlike services warranty of meaningful duration with a repair-or-refund remedy, and that an 'AS IS' disclaimer does not swallow the affirmative warranty.

Insurance covenants are often omitted from short vendor-form MSAs; check the general provisions and any exhibit. Given Kubient handles AP data, expect commercial general liability, professional/tech E&O and cyber cover with certificates on request — mark missing if no such covenant exists anywhere.

Presence check. Minimum spend, impression or volume commitments would sit in the fees section or an order form/exhibit rather than the preamble. Flag only a take-or-pay style commitment with no termination or true-up exit for AP.

Check the effects-of-termination/survival provisions for return or deletion of AP data in a usable format and reasonable wind-down assistance. Vendor forms often cover deletion only; if there is no data-return or transition obligation at all, treat as missing.
